title: MiniCall
summary: A call that continues while people do something else is shown in the system's picture-in-picture window. Monarch ships no floating call window.
whenToUse: To keep a video call visible when the person leaves the call screen or the app: enter picture in picture from the call activity, and hide the controls while the activity is in picture in picture.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a draggable in-app window; it cannot leave the app and duplicates the system one. For an audio-only call the ongoing call notification is enough.

options.name: aspectRatio
options.description: The shape of the window, for example 16:9 for a shared screen or 9:16 for a phone camera.

options.name: autoEnterEnabled
options.description: Android 12 and later: enters picture in picture when the person goes home, without a button.

states.name: full screen
states.description: The call activity with all its controls.

states.name: picture in picture
states.description: The same activity in a small system window; the app hides its controls and the system draws its own.

appearance: The system draws the window, its frame and its controls. The content inside is the app's call screen in the Monarch theme, without its controls.
platformNotes: The web MiniCall is a draggable in-page window with a timer, mute, expand and leave. Android uses its own picture-in-picture mode, as iOS uses AVPictureInPictureController. Mute and leave stay on the call screen, in the ongoing call notification, or as RemoteAction items set with PictureInPictureParams.Builder.setActions. The activity must declare android:supportsPictureInPicture="true" in the manifest.
accessibility: System behavior: the picture-in-picture window is accessible and can be moved, expanded and closed with TalkBack.
Give the button that starts it a visible label, such as "Continue in picture in picture".
edgeCases: Picture in picture needs Android 8 (API 26); check Build.VERSION.SDK_INT and PackageManager.FEATURE_PICTURE_IN_PICTURE.
Without android:supportsPictureInPicture in the manifest, enterPictureInPictureMode throws IllegalStateException.
The whole activity goes into the window, so a call screen is usually its own activity.

The example and the catalogue page were compiled and composed; the window was not opened on a device. The catalogue activity declares picture in picture with the configuration changes it handles; its page sets setAutoEnterEnabled and setSourceRectHint on Android 12 and later while it is open.
